perspective:
**Mason Hurley’s available information:**

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center; Martha Moua is a personal care aide colleague there. Their relationship is professional and mainly work-related.
- He reviewed financial reports and noticed discrepancies, especially unusually high healthcare expenses. This led him to suspect Martha might be mismanaging funds, making him suspicious and anxious.
- He spoke with Martha, asked to discuss the report, said the numbers did not add up, and pointed to the healthcare expenses. He heard Martha say there may have been a misentry, and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, he learned the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved and embarrassed, apologized for his initial suspicion, and heard Martha say errors happen, she understood his thoroughness, and they should double-check entries next time.
- He came to believe Martha was competent, but that the recurring clerical errors showed the financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- He discussed prevention with Martha, said the issue was not her management but the current system, proposed a new, more robust financial system, and said he would draft a proposal with her input. He heard Martha agree and offer to help.
- He drafted the proposal and felt hopeful but uncertain whether management would approve or implement it. He told Martha he finished the draft and was unsure how management would receive it. He heard Martha call it solid, encourage confidence, and agree to help gather data when he asked.
- He presented the proposal to management. He felt satisfied with his efforts but physically and mentally exhausted, and believed he had done everything possible to advocate for the new system.
- He told Martha the presentation went well and it was now up to management. He heard Martha praise him and suggest taking time off. He thanked her, said he would take a few days off to recharge and reflect, and hoped for good news.
- He is waiting for management’s decision after the presentation.
